topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Closer CPU
explanation: The memory hierarchy organizes storage based on speed, size, and cost, positioning smaller, faster cache levels (L1, L2, L3) closest to the CPU core. This proximity minimizes access latency, ensuring the CPU primarily interacts with the fastest available memory. Caching strategies exploit locality of reference—both temporal (reusing recent data) and spatial (accessing nearby data)—by predicting and staging frequently accessed blocks into these high-speed buffers. A successful cache hit allows data retrieval at near-register speeds, drastically reducing the effective memory access time and maximizing system throughput. Conversely, a cache miss forces the CPU to fetch data from slower main memory (DRAM), incurring a significant performance penalty.
